changes.reason: つぶつぶと describes small lumps or clumps of cloud, and “clumps” preserves that shape in English.

changes.find: every field that is a field, hemp or millet, hangs its head limply in the rising heat from the earth
changes.reason: “Every field” already carries the totalising force of 畑と云ふ畑 without requiring the English reader to parse the repetition literally.
changes.replace: every field, hemp or millet, hangs its head limply in the heat rising from the earth

changes.find: Then a handy unglazed earthen jar is set at this man's pillow,
changes.reason: 手ごろな means conveniently sized, and “handy-sized” makes that sense clear.
changes.replace: Then a handy-sized unglazed earthen jar is set at this man's pillow,

changes.find: squats there portentously, in the attitude of a turkey.
changes.reason: 勿体らしく denotes self-importance rather than menace, so this keeps the monk pompous and comic without making him ominous.
changes.replace: squats there with an air of importance, in the attitude of a turkey.

changes.find: grows only a perfunctory beard like a rat's tail on the tip of his chin,
changes.reason: 申訳だけに means that the beard is only token, and “token beard” conveys that slightness naturally.
changes.replace: sports only a token beard, like a rat's tail, on the tip of his chin,

changes.find: he preciously plies a fan made of white birds' feathers,
changes.reason: 大事さうに describes the care with which Sun handles the fan, and the replacement states that directly.
changes.replace: he handles a fan made of white birds' feathers with great care,

changes.find: leaning against a bamboo wife and fighting out a game on the board,
changes.reason: “Bamboo-wife bolster” identifies the object just enough for the action and setting to be understood without a longer explanation.
changes.replace: leaning against a bamboo-wife bolster and playing out a game on the board,

changes.find: I have come to cure your disease.
changes.reason: 貧道 is the monk’s marked clerical self-reference, and “This poor monk” retains its claim to authority while keeping his speech abrupt.
changes.replace: This poor monk has come to cure your disease.

changes.find: he had an unglazed earthen jar filled with wine brought to Liu's pillow.
changes.reason: 酒を入れた says that wine was put in the jar, not that it was filled, and avoiding “filled” also preserves the later imagined brimming from being anticipated.
changes.replace: he had an unglazed earthen jar with wine in it brought to Liu's pillow.

changes.find: Over the whole surface of the skin a force is at work tending to move in every direction, while the skin itself has not the least elasticity against it.
changes.reason: The Japanese describes a bodily pull in every direction met by skin with no elasticity, and “tugs” with “no give” keeps that sensation immediate.
changes.replace: Across every inch of skin something tugs in every direction at once, and the skin has no give in it at all.

changes.find: From the mouth of the jar the heavy smell of wine comes without break to assail his nose.
changes.reason: 芬々たる酒香 is richly fragrant, and its pleasantness is part of what makes the wine torment Liu while retaining the repeated word “smell.”
changes.replace: From the mouth of the jar the rich fragrant smell of wine comes without break to assail his nose.

changes.find: suddenly raised the haunches he had settled
changes.reason: The Japanese has the monk raise himself from his settled squat, and the replacement gives that movement without the distracting anatomical phrase.
changes.replace: suddenly heaved himself up from where he had settled

changes.find: frost-touched hair at the temples lingers only faintly above the temples,
changes.reason: 双髩 and 顳顬 distinguish the side hair from the temples, but English can carry both with one reference here without repeating the same word.
changes.replace: frost-touched hair at the temples survives only faintly,

changes.find: if the spitting out of the wine worm and Liu's later destitution are set side by side in a relation of cause and effect, this is a question apt to occur to anyone.
changes.reason: The replacement preserves the causal juxtaposition and the dry questioning while removing the nominalised construction that obscured them.
changes.replace: once you set the spitting-out of the wine worm side by side with Liu's later ruin as cause and effect, it is a question anyone would ask.

changes.find: that the health and estate of the Liu of former days should have been lost is entirely natural, and a matter of course.
changes.reason: 至極、当然な話 is a single closing formula, and the single English predicate keeps the third answer from outweighing the other two.
changes.replace: that the health and estate of the Liu of former days should have been lost would be only natural.

declined.reason: うるささうに presents the hair as hanging in a way that seems to trouble its wearer, whereas “straggling unkempt” changes that suggestion into a judgement on its appearance.
The proposed wording retains the same fronted construction while “ended up” adds a casualness not present in 当座の行きがかりで, so it does not materially improve the sentence.

disagreements.choice: “squats there with an air of importance, in the attitude of a turkey.”
disagreements.faithful_side: F2 objects that “portentously” makes 勿体らしく ominous and proposes “with an air of importance.”
disagreements.readable_side: R4 also objects that “portentously” conflicts with the comic simile and proposes “with ponderous self-importance.”

data.say: The desk retained the tale’s undecided moral balance by removing wording that made the monk ominous, expanded the third answer, or softened the pleasurable smell that torments Liu.
